subject: Provider verification must be decomposed into licensure, payer participation, discovery metadata, and fresh availability observations
summary: BC regulatory registries are strongest for current professional licence/status but carry source-use restrictions requiring production terms/licensing review.
CHCPBC and CCHPBC licence-number migrations during 2026 require versioned regulator identifier aliases rather than licence number as the Provider primary key.
TELUS eClaims, Canada Life, and Pacific Blue Cross provide payer/direct-billing participation signals but do not prove a specific member plan will cover a specific service.

Jane exposes real-time bookable openings for opted-in clinics in its current BC Practitioner Search beta, while Sun Life Provider Search exposes richer discovery/availability data with explicit completeness and freshness disclaimers.
Directory absence is not reliable negative evidence; privacy suppression, opt-in scope, and source incompleteness must be represented explicitly.

The current Beta Provider and ProviderVerification models are too coarse for production trust and should split identity, licensure, payer participation, availability, and plan-specific verification into provenance-bearing observations.
